classification.difficultyReason: Decide which surfaces are painted (wall and lid, no base), compute πr²+2πrh, divide by the coverage and round up the number of cans. The structure matches the pool problem.

content.prompt:
Hamid is painting a closed cylindrical water tank.
The curved wall and the lid are to be painted, but not the base.
If a one-litre can of paint covers $15\text{ m}^2$, find the number of cans needed.

answer.worked:
The base is not painted; paint the curved wall and the circular lid.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\pi rh+\pi r^2\\A&=2\pi(2.5)(6)+\pi(2.5)^2\\A&=36.25\pi\text{ m}^2\approx113.9\text{ m}^2\\\text{Paint required}&=\frac{113.9}{15}\approx7.6\text{ L}\end{align*}$$
Round up to buy enough paint: $8$ one-litre cans.
